# Glossary authoring contract {#sec-glossary-authoring}

Technical books need one durable definition for a term even when the term is
referenced in several chapters, forms, or editions. Alkahest stores that source
once in `glossary.yml`; manuscript prose selects a stable semantic name and a
display form without copying the definition.

## Terms, acronyms, and first use {#sec-glossary-forms}

A {{< alk-term central-processing-unit >}} fetches, decodes, and executes
instructions. This later chapter may use {{< alk-term cpu form=acronym >}}
without hard-coding either expansion, proving that cross-chapter references
retain one identity. A multiprocessor discussion may refer to several
{{< alk-term cpu form=acronym-plural >}}. When the full plural is clearer, the
same entry emits {{< alk-term central-processing-unit form=plural >}}.

The {{< alk-term instruction-set-architecture form=first >}} defines the
programmer-visible processor contract. The `isa` alias still resolves to the
canonical registry identity when rendered as {{< alk-term isa form=acronym >}}.

Irregular forms are data rather than author memory: one
{{< alk-term matrix form=first >}} may become several
{{< alk-term matrix form=plural >}}, while a later reference to the
{{< alk-term matrix >}} keeps the registered singular. An entry may also mark a
plural first use explicitly, as in
{{< alk-term quantum-bit form=first-plural >}}.

## Authoring syntax {#sec-glossary-syntax}

The first positional argument is a stable registry ID or alias. The optional
`form` is one of `term`, `plural`, `acronym`, `acronym-plural`, `first`, or
`first-plural`; omitted `form` means `term`. `case=sentence` performs a
Unicode-aware first-letter capitalization, and `link=false` is an explicit
escape hatch when a reflowable link would be distracting.

```{.markdown shortcodes=false}
{{< alk-term central-processing-unit form=first >}}
{{< alk-term cpu form=acronym >}}
{{< alk-term matrix form=plural >}}
{{< alk-term matrix link=false >}}
```

`first` and `first-plural` are explicit editorial markers. This avoids hidden
state: split HTML chapters, an EPUB, and a whole-book PDF all render the same
wording even when an edition later omits earlier chapters. A validator rejects
unknown IDs, aliases, forms, unavailable plural/acronym data, and duplicate
explicit first-use markers.

The fallback remains semantic visible text without a hyperlink, as demonstrated
by [{{< alk-term matrix link=false >}}]{#glossary-unlinked-fallback}. Print
outputs use the same visible fallback for every occurrence and put navigation
in the generated first-use page references.

## Generated back matter {#sec-glossary-back-matter}

The back-matter placeholder builds the book's glossary once from the registry.
Entries sort by their displayed term and retain stable ID-derived anchors.
HTML and EPUB term references link to those entries and expose the definition as
supplementary hover text. Typst and LuaLaTeX glossary entries report the page of
the explicit first-use marker, so pagination is calculated by each print engine
rather than copied into source.
